methodology.question_set_source: 00_ARCHITECTURE/llm_consumption_audit/ledgers/elevation_v2/DARK_CORPUS_REPLAY_SET_v1_0.json (status: FROZEN) — the exact G15-referenced 21-question dark-corpus replay set. methodology.prior_measurement_found: 00_ARCHITECTURE/llm_consumption_audit/capability_map/DARK_CORPUS_REPORT_v1_0.md (+ .json), Elevation Campaign v2.1 Stream gamma, original run 2026-07-25, ADDENDUM 2026-07-28 post-PARISHODHANA re-measurement.
methodology.original_rubric_not_replicated: The ORIGINAL Omega-7 harness rubric is NOT a qualitative bright/dark read of each answer's prose. It is a concept-level coverage metric: bright% = (count of the chart's full computed/stored L1-L5 concept universe for the domain, e.g. 12,450 concepts for wealth) that were matched — via exact fact_id or distinguishing-token string match against the UNION of all 21 raw tool-call transcripts — divided into that same universe. Replicating it exactly requires (a) a live Postgres connection to regenerate the served-concept denominator via platform/scripts/census/generate_completeness_accounting.mjs, and (b) running the sealed evals/omega7/build_report.py + darkcorpus_match.py graders against transcripts captured in their exact expected JSON shape. That full concept-universe apparatus was judged out of proportion for a single read-only audit agent's pass and was NOT re-run here. This run therefore uses the TASK'S OWN FALLBACK RUBRIC instead (see below) — a qualitative per-answer bright/dark grade, not a concept-coverage percentage. THE TWO BRIGHT% NUMBERS BELOW ARE THEREFORE NOT THE SAME METRIC — see 'baseline_comparison.metric_comparability' for the explicit disclosure.

grading_rubric_used.bright: Most of: (a) cites specific L1 fact_ids/citation_ref strings or classical text references (BPHS chapter/verse etc); (b) content differentiated to THIS chart's actual computed values (real signs/houses/degrees/named yogas/strength numbers for Abhisek Mohanty), not boilerplate that could describe any chart; (c) calibrated/epistemic language (verdict grades, structural_prior/epistemic tags, judgment_flags disclosing gaps) rather than absolute fortune-telling claims; (d) acharya-grade depth (dignity chains, bhanga/cancellation state, multi-varga confirmation, dasha timing, cross-source convergence). For expert-band questions specifically, a response is graded DARK if it never actually engages the specific named technique (dispositor chain / bhavat-bhavam / sudarshana-chakra / mutual reception / etc) even when the substituted content is itself well-cited — a well-grounded non-answer to the question asked is still a dark result for THIS question.
grading_rubric_used.dark: Any of: generic boilerplate applicable to any chart; no fact citations; error/timeout/empty response; hollow non-answer; OR (expert band) a well-cited but off-topic substitution that evades the specific expert technique named in the question.

methodology.execution_method: Live MCP tool calls (mcp__marsys-jis-direct__* namespace) issued directly against the running server for each of the 21 questions, split across three parallel sub-agents by phrasing band (naive/narrow/expert) to keep per-call context manageable; each sub-agent chose its own tool(s) per question the way a competent routing layer would, called them live, and graded the raw response.
methodology.scope_note: Wealth domain only (21/21 questions). Career domain's parallel 21-question set (DC-C-01..21) exists in the same frozen replay set but was NOT re-run in this pass — resource-scoped to one full domain rather than a partial sample across both, matching the original artifact's own full-domain-at-a-time reporting unit.

The two numbers should NOT be read as 'quality regressed from 5.58% to 90.48%' or vice versa; they measure different things.
